chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) and 'Uthman differed regarding a man who dies and has no 'asabah (agnates) to inherit him, but has a close relative who does not inherit.
Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance is for them,' citing God's saying: 'And those of kinship among each other are nearer [to one another] in the Book of Allah.'
And 'Uthman said: 'It is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.أُولُوا اَلْأَرْحامِ: Those of kinship / Those of the wombs (referring to close relatives)
key_terms.بَيْتُ مَالِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ: The treasury of the Muslims / Public treasury
key_terms.ذُو قَرَابَةٍ: Close relative (a general term for kin, often used here to denote those who are not 'asabah)
key_terms.عَصَبَةٌ: Agnatic heirs (male relatives who inherit by virtue of their male lineage, excluding females and those with female links)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Imam Ali's and 'Uthman's ruling on inheritance for those with no agnatic heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights a foundational jurisprudential dispute between Imam Ali and Caliph Uthman regarding the inheritance of a deceased with no agnatic heirs ('asabah) but with other close relatives (dhawu al-qarabah). Imam Ali advocated for the relatives based on the principle of 'qurb' (kinship closeness) derived from Surah Al-Nisa, while Uthman favored allocating the estate to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). This difference underscores the Shia emphasis on the Quranic text of 'qurb' as a primary basis for inheritance, contrasting with the Sunni preference for the 'asabah' system in such cases.
